text:
deploy-bot: starting rollout release-4.0.0 -> canary (10%) us-west2 at 7755123456. watching p95, error-rate, routing-tag-consistency. autopilot: auto_revert=true for rerank route only; other routes notify-only.
nina: noticed unusual traffic in dedicated-pool-us at 7755123460. looks like canary traffic spilled into dedicated-reserved because route tag 'service=search' misapplied. dash: https://internal.metrics/redwood/4.0.0/overview
carlos: who tagged that deploy? I thought relmanager applied tags per-route. this might be a relmanager->router mismatch.
zane-oncall: if dedicated customers see canary, we should act fast. autopilot won't cover dedicated since reserved pools are manual. options: (A) immediate pin of dedicated pool back to 3.9.x (B) remove mis-tag so routing respects canary scope (C) targeted traffic-set to re-route dedicated-hosted traffic to stable variant.
nina: quick check: `redwoodctl routing show --pool=dedicated-pool-us` shows release=4.0.0 for route=search for a subset of tenants. definitely mis-routed.
carlos: I recommend option C + pin for affected tenants. less risk than flipping global tags. we can bring dedicated traffic back to 3.9.7 for only affected allocations.
pm-amy: heads up: two enterprise accounts (Acme & BetaCo) on dedicated-pool-us. sales needs a one-liner if we contact them.
sales-bot: created note: "Notifying Acme & BetaCo - small subset of traffic routed to a canary; investigating; no data loss reported." queued to account teams.
zane-oncall: action list: 1) nina run targeted traffic-set to move affected allocations to 3.9.7 2) carlos pin those tenant allocations 3) pm-amy coordinate account comms 4) open postmortem ticket. ack?
nina: ack. executing: `redwoodctl rollout traffic-set --scope=allocation:acme,beta --route=search --target=3.9.7 --canary=0`
carlos: pin command ready: `redwoodctl versions pin --scope=allocation:acme,beta --route=search --version=3.9.7 --reason "mis-routed canary traffic on release-4.0.0"`
nina: traffic-set completed 7755123468. allocations moved to 3.9.7.
carlos: pin applied 7755123470. `redwoodctl show pins --scope=allocation:acme,beta` returns pins active.
pm-amy: customer note drafted: "We've reverted the search route for your dedicated allocation to the previous stable version due to an internal routing misconfiguration during a canary. No data impact. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA." sending now.
sales-bot: messages sent to account teams 7755123472.
zane-oncall: we also need to patch relmanager->router tagging flow. carlos, can you open PR & a short rollback test?
carlos: opening PR with a guard: reject routing changes that set release=canary on dedicated allocations unless explicit flag `--allow-dedicated=true`. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/7890. will add unit tests.
nina: metrics on pinned allocations look normal at 7755123474. p95 back to baseline.
pm-amy: legal cc'ed for enterprise notices. am confirming if either account wants an NBD (no big deal) or a formal statement.
zane-oncall: created postmortem ticket RED-8001 and assigned to carlos for infra RCA and nina for mitigation timeline. please include timeline and tests to prevent future mis-tagging.
pm-amy: final status update for tracker: targeted mitigation executed, affected dedicated allocations pinned to 3.9.7, customer account teams notified, PR open to gate dedicated routing. RCA ETA 72h. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollout log updated: events: traffic_set=7755123468 pin=7755123470 customer_notify=7755123472 postmortem=7755123475.
nina: thanks team, closing this thread and moving details into RED-8001 and release tracker.
